잠언-1-2.exegesis: INTRODUCTION I. The Nature and Use of Proverbs.-- A proverb is a pithy sentence, concisely expressing some well-established truth susceptible of various illustrations and applications. The word is of Latin derivation, literally meaning for a word, speech, or discourse; that is, one expression for many. The Hebrew word for "proverb" (mashal) means a "comparison." Many suppose it was used, because the form or matter of the proverb, or both, involved the idea of comparison. Most of the proverbs are in couplets or triplets, or some modifications of them, the members of which correspond in structure and length, as if arranged to be compared one with another. They illustrate the varieties of parallelism, a distinguishing feature of Hebrew poetry. Compare Introduction to Poetical Books. Many also clearly involve the idea of comparison in the sentiments expressed (compare Pr 12:1-10; 25 :10-15; 26:1-9). Sometimes, however, the designed omission of one member of the comparison, exercising the reader's sagacity or study for its supply, presents the proverb as a "riddle" or "dark saying" (compare Pr 30:15-33; 1:6; Psa 49:4 ). The sententious form of expression, which thus became a marked feature of the proverbial style, was also adopted for continuous discourse, even when not always preserving traces of comparison, either in form or matter (compare Pr 1: 1-9:18 ). In Eze 17:1 ; 24:3 , we find the same word properly translated "parable," to designate an illustrative discourse. Then the Greek translators have used a word, parabola ("parable"), which the gospel writers (except John) employ for our Lord's discourses of the same character, and which also seems to involve the idea of comparison, though that may not be its primary meaning. It might seem, therefore, that the proverbial and parabolic styles of writing were originally and essentially the same. The proverb is a "concentrated parable, and the parable an extension of the proverb by a full illustration." The proverb is thus the moral or theme of a parable, which sometimes precedes it, as in Mt 19:30 (compare Pr 20:1 ); or succeeds it, as in Mt 22:1-16 ; Lu 15:1-10 . The style being poetical, and adapted to the expression of a high order of poetical sentiment, such as prophecy, we find the same term used to designate such compositions (compare Nu 23:7 ; Mi 2:4 ; Ha 2:6 ). Though the Hebrews used the same term for proverb and parable, the Greek employs two, though the sacred writers have not always appeared to recognize a distinction. The term for proverb is, paroimia, which the Greek translators employ for the title of this book, evidently with special reference to the later definition of a proverb, as a trite, sententious form of speech, which appears to be the best meaning of the term. John uses the same term to designate our Saviour's instructions, in view of their characteristic obscurity (compare Pr 16:25-29 , Greek), and even for his illustrative discourses ( Pr 10:6 ), whose sense was not at once obvious to all his hearers. This form of instruction was well adapted to aid the learner. The parallel structure of sentences, the repetition, contrast, or comparison of thought, were all calculated to facilitate the efforts of memory; and precepts of practical wisdom which, extended into logical discourses, might have failed to make abiding impressions by reason of their length or complicated character, were thus compressed into pithy, and, for the most part, very plain statements. Such a mode of instruction has distinguished the written or traditional literature of all nations, and was, and still is, peculiarly current in the East. In this book, however, we are supplied with a proverbial wisdom commended by the seal of divine inspiration. God has condescended to become our teacher on the practical affairs belonging to all the relations of life. He has adapted His instruction to the plain and unlettered, and presented, in this striking and impressive method, the great principles of duty to Him and to our fellow men. To the prime motive of all right conduct, the fear of God, are added all lawful and subordinate incentives, such as honor, interest, love, fear, and natural affection. Besides the terror excited by an apprehension of God's justly provoked judgments, we are warned against evil-doing by the exhibition of the inevitable temporal results of impiety, injustice, profligacy, idleness, laziness, indolence, drunkenness, and debauchery. To the rewards of true piety which follow in eternity, are promised the peace, security, love, and approbation of the good, and the comforts of a clear conscience, which render this life truly happy. II. Inspiration and Authorship.-- With no important exception, Jewish and Christian writers have received this book as the inspired production of Solomon. It is the first book of the Bible prefaced by the name of the author. The New Testament abounds with citations from the Proverbs. Its intrinsic excellence commends it to us as the production of a higher authority than the apocryphal writings, such as Wisdom or Ecclesiasticus. Solomon lived five hundred years before the "seven wise men" of Greece, and seven hundred before the age of Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle. It is thus very evident, whatever theory of his sources of knowledge be adopted, that he did not draw upon any heathen repositories with which we are acquainted. It is far more probable, that by the various migrations, captivities, and dispersions of the Jews, heathen philosophers drew from this inspired fountain many of those streams which continue to refresh mankind amid the otherwise barren and parched deserts of profane literature. As, however, the Psalms are ascribed to David, because he was the leading author, so the ascription of this book to Solomon is entirely consistent with the titles of the thirtieth and thirty-first chapters, which assign those chapters to Agur and Lemuel respectively. Of these persons we know nothing. This is not the place for discussing the various speculations respecting them. By a slight change of reading some propose to translate Pr 30:1 : "The words of Agur, the son of her who was obeyed Massa," that is, "the queen of Massa"; and Pr 31:1 : "The words of Lemuel, king of Massa"; but to this the earliest versions are contradictory, and nothing other than the strongest exegetical necessity ought to be allowed to justify a departure from a well-established reading and version when nothing useful to our knowledge is gained. It is better to confess ignorance than indulge in useless conjectures. It is probable that out of the "three thousand proverbs" ( 1Ki 4:32 ) which Solomon spoke, he selected and edited Pr 1:1-24:34 during his life. Pr 25:1-29:27 were also of his production, and copied out in the days of Hezekiah, by his "men," perhaps the prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah. Such a work was evidently in the spirit of this pious monarch, who set his heart so fully on a reformation of God's worship. Learned men have endeavored to establish the theory that Solomon himself was only a collector; or that the other parts of the book, as these chapters, were also selections by later hands; but the reasons adduced to maintain these views have never appeared so satisfactory as to change the usual opinions on the subject, which have the sanction of the most ancient and reliable authorities. III. Divisions of the Book.-- Such a work is, of course, not susceptible of any logical analysis. There are, however, some well-defined marks of division, so that very generally the book is divided into five or six parts. 1. The first contains nine chapters, in which are discussed and enforced by illustration, admonition, and encouragement the principles and blessings of wisdom, and the pernicious schemes and practices of sinful persons. These chapters are introductory. With few specimens of the proper proverb, they are distinguished by its conciseness and terseness. The sentences follow very strictly the form of parallelism, and generally of the synonymous species, only forty of the synthetic and four ( Pr 3:32-35 ) of the antithetic appearing. The style is ornate, the figures bolder and fuller, and the illustrations more striking and extended. 2. The antithetic and synthetic parallelism to the exclusion of the synonymous distinguish Pr 10:1-22:16, and the verses are entirely unconnected, each containing a complete sense in itself. 3. Pr 22:16-24:34 present a series of admonitions as if addressed to a pupil, and generally each topic occupies two or more verses. 4. Pr 25:1-29:27 are entitled to be regarded as a distinct portion, for the reason given above as to its origin. The style is very much mixed; of the peculiarities, compare parts two and three. 5. Pr 30:1-33 is peculiar not only for its authorship, but as a specimen of the kind of proverb which has been described as "dark sayings" or "riddles." 6. To a few pregnant but concise admonitions, suitable for a king, is added a most inimitable portraiture of female character. In both parts five and six the distinctive peculiarity of the original proverbial style gives place to the modifications already mentioned as marking a later composition, though both retain the concise and nervous method of stating truth, equally valuable for its deep impression and permanent retention by the memory. CHAPTER 1 Pr 1:1-33 . After the title the writer defines the design and nature of the instructions of the book. He paternally invites attention to those instructions and warns his readers against the enticements of the wicked. In a beautiful personification, wisdom is then introduced in a most solemn and impressive manner, publicly inviting men to receive its teachings, warning those who reject, and encouraging those who accept, the proffered instructions. 1-4. (See Introduction, Part I).

잠언-1-5.theologicalNote: INTRODUCTION I. The Nature and Use of Proverbs.-- A proverb is a pithy sentence, concisely expressing some well-established truth susceptible of various illustrations and applications. The word is of Latin derivation, literally meaning for a word, speech, or discourse; that is, one expression for many. The Hebrew word for "proverb" (mashal) means a "comparison." Many suppose it was used, because the form or matter of the proverb, or both, involved the idea of comparison. Most of the proverbs are in couplets or triplets, or some modifications of them, the members of which correspond in structure and length, as if arranged to be compared one with another. They illustrate the varieties of parallelism, a distinguishing feature of Hebrew poetry. Compare Introduction to Poetical Books. Many also clearly involve the idea of comparison in the sentiments expressed (compare Pr 12:1-10; 25 :10-15; 26:1-9). Sometimes, however, the designed omission of one member of the comparison, exercising the reader's sagacity or study for its supply, presents the proverb as a "riddle" or "dark saying" (compare Pr 30:15-33; 1:6; Psa 49:4 ). The sententious form of expression, which thus became a marked feature of the proverbial style, was also adopted for continuous discourse, even when not always preserving traces of comparison, either in form or matter (compare Pr 1: 1-9:18 ). In Eze 17:1 ; 24:3 , we find the same word properly translated "parable," to designate an illustrative discourse. Then the Greek translators have used a word, parabola ("parable"), which the gospel writers (except John) employ for our Lord's discourses of the same character, and which also seems to involve the idea of comparison, though that may not be its primary meaning. It might seem, therefore, that the proverbial and parabolic styles of writing were originally and essentially the same. The proverb is a "concentrated parable, and the parable an extension of the proverb by a full illustration." The proverb is thus the moral or theme of a parable, which sometimes precedes it, as in Mt 19:30 (compare Pr 20:1 ); or succeeds it, as in Mt 22:1-16 ; Lu 15:1-10 . The style being poetical, and adapted to the expression of a high order of poetical sentiment, such as prophecy, we find the same term used to designate such compositions (compare Nu 23:7 ; Mi 2:4 ; Ha 2:6 ). Though the Hebrews used the same term for proverb and parable, the Greek employs two, though the sacred writers have not always appeared to recognize a distinction. The term for proverb is, paroimia, which the Greek translators employ for the title of this book, evidently with special reference to the later definition of a proverb, as a trite, sententious form of speech, which appears to be the best meaning of the term. John uses the same term to designate our Saviour's instructions, in view of their characteristic obscurity (compare Pr 16:25-29 , Greek), and even for his illustrative discourses ( Pr 10:6 ), whose sense was not at once obvious to all his hearers. This form of instruction was well adapted to aid the learner. The parallel structure of sentences, the repetition, contrast, or comparison of thought, were all calculated to facilitate the efforts of memory; and precepts of practical wisdom which, extended into logical discourses, might have failed to make abiding impressions by reason of their length or complicated character, were thus compressed into pithy, and, for the most part, very plain statements. Such a mode of instruction has distinguished the written or traditional literature of all nations, and was, and still is, peculiarly current in the East. In this book, however, we are supplied with a proverbial wisdom commended by the seal of divine inspiration. God has condescended to become our teacher on the practical affairs belonging to all the relations of life. He has adapted His instruction to the plain and unlettered, and presented, in this striking and impressive method, the great principles of duty to Him and to our fellow men. To the prime motive of all right conduct, the fear of God, are added all lawful and subordinate incentives, such as honor, interest, love, fear, and natural affection. Besides the terror excited by an apprehension of God's justly provoked judgments, we are warned against evil-doing by the exhibition of the inevitable temporal results of impiety, injustice, profligacy, idleness, laziness, indolence, drunkenness, and debauchery. To the rewards of true piety which follow in eternity, are promised the peace, security, love, and approbation of the good, and the comforts of a clear conscience, which render this life truly happy. II. Inspiration and Authorship.-- With no important exception, Jewish and Christian writers have received this book as the inspired production of Solomon. It is the first book of the Bible prefaced by the name of the author. The New Testament abounds with citations from the Proverbs. Its intrinsic excellence commends it to us as the production of a higher authority than the apocryphal writings, such as Wisdom or Ecclesiasticus. Solomon lived five hundred years before the "seven wise men" of Greece, and seven hundred before the age of Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle. It is thus very evident, whatever theory of his sources of knowledge be adopted, that he did not draw upon any heathen repositories with which we are acquainted. It is far more probable, that by the various migrations, captivities, and dispersions of the Jews, heathen philosophers drew from this inspired fountain many of those streams which continue to refresh mankind amid the otherwise barren and parched deserts of profane literature. As, however, the Psalms are ascribed to David, because he was the leading author, so the ascription of this book to Solomon is entirely consistent with the titles of the thirtieth and thirty-first chapters, which assign those chapters to Agur and Lemuel respectively. Of these persons we know nothing. This is not the place for discussing the various speculations respecting them. By a slight change of reading some propose to translate Pr 30:1 : "The words of Agur, the son of her who was obeyed Massa," that is, "the queen of Massa"; and Pr 31:1 : "The words of Lemuel, king of Massa"; but to this the earliest versions are contradictory, and nothing other than the strongest exegetical necessity ought to be allowed to justify a departure from a well-established reading and version when nothing useful to our knowledge is gained. It is better to confess ignorance than indulge in useless conjectures. It is probable that out of the "three thousand proverbs" ( 1Ki 4:32 ) which Solomon spoke, he selected and edited Pr 1:1-24:34 during his life. Pr 25:1-29:27 were also of his production, and copied out in the days of Hezekiah, by his "men," perhaps the prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah. Such a work was evidently in the spirit of this pious monarch, who set his heart so fully on a reformation of God's worship. Learned men have endeavored to establish the theory that Solomon himself was only a collector; or that the other parts of the book, as these chapters, were also selections by later hands; but the reasons adduced to maintain these views have never appeared so satisfactory as to change the usual opinions on the subject, which have the sanction of the most ancient and reliable authorities. III. Divisions of the Book.-- Such a work is, of course, not susceptible of any logical analysis. There are, however, some well-defined marks of division, so that very generally the book is divided into five or six parts. 1. The first contains nine chapters, in which are discussed and enforced by illustration, admonition, and encouragement the principles and blessings of wisdom, and the pernicious schemes and practices of sinful persons. These chapters are introductory. With few specimens of the proper proverb, they are distinguished by its conciseness and terseness. The sentences follow very strictly the form of parallelism, and generally of the synonymous species, only forty of the synthetic and four ( Pr 3:32-35 ) of the antithetic appearing. The style is ornate, the figures bolder and fuller, and the illustrations more striking and extended. 2. The antithetic and synthetic parallelism to the exclusion of the synonymous distinguish Pr 10:1-22:16, and the verses are entirely unconnected, each containing a complete sense in itself. 3. Pr 22:16-24:34 present a series of admonitions as if addressed to a pupil, and generally each topic occupies two or more verses. 4. Pr 25:1-29:27 are entitled to be regarded as a distinct portion, for the reason given above as to its origin. The style is very much mixed; of the peculiarities, compare parts two and three. 5. Pr 30:1-33 is peculiar not only for its authorship, but as a specimen of the kind of proverb which has been described as "dark sayings" or "riddles." 6. To a few pregnant but concise admonitions, suitable for a king, is added a most inimitable portraiture of female character. In both parts five and six the distinctive peculiarity of the original proverbial style gives place to the modifications already mentioned as marking a later composition, though both retain the concise and nervous method of stating truth, equally valuable for its deep impression and permanent retention by the memory. CHAPTER 1 Pr 1:1-33 . After the title the writer defines the design and nature of the instructions of the book. He paternally invites attention to those instructions and warns his readers against the enticements of the wicked. In a beautiful personification, wisdom is then introduced in a most solemn and impressive manner, publicly inviting men to receive its teachings, warning those who reject, and encouraging those who accept, the proffered instructions. 1-4. (See Introduction, Part I).

잠언-2-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 2 Pr 2:1-22 . Men are invited to seek wisdom because it teaches those principles by which they may obtain God's guidance and avoid the society and influence of the wicked, whose pernicious courses are described. 1-5. Diligence in hearing and praying for instruction must be used to secure the great principle of godliness, the fear of God. hide ... with thee-- lay up in store (compare Pr 7:1 ).

잠언-6-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 6 Pr 6:1-35 . After admonitions against suretyship and sloth (compare Pr 6:6-8 ), the character and fate of the wicked generally are set forth, and the writer ( Pr 6:20-35 ) resumes the warnings against incontinence, pointing out its certain and terrible results. This train of thought seems to intimate the kindred of these vices. 1-2. if-- The condition extends through both verses. be surety-- art pledged. stricken ... hand-- bargained (compare Job 17:3 ). with a stranger-- that is, for a friend (compare Pr 11:15 ; 17:18 ).

잠언-8-2.title: 잠언 8장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-8-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 8 Pr 8:1-36 . Contrasted with sensual allurements are the advantages of divine wisdom, which publicly invites men, offers the best principles of life, and the most valuable benefits resulting from receiving her counsels. Her relation to the divine plans and acts is introduced, as in Pr 3:19 , 20 , though more fully, to commend her desirableness for men, and the whole is closed by an assurance that those finding her find God's favor, and those neglecting ruin themselves. Many regard the passage as a description of the Son of God by the title, Wisdom, which the older Jews used (and by which He is called in Lu 11:49 ), as Joh 1:1 , &c., describes Him by that of Logos, the Word. But the passage may be taken as a personification of wisdom: for, (1) Though described as with God, wisdom is not asserted to be God. (2) The use of personal attributes is equally consistent with a personification, as with the description of a real person. (3) The personal pronouns used accord with the gender (feminine) of wisdom constantly, and are never changed to that of the person meant, as sometimes occurs in a corresponding use of spirit, which is neuter in Greek, but to which masculine pronouns are often applied ( Joh 16:14 ), when the acts of the Holy Spirit are described. (4) Such a personification is agreeable to the style of this book (compare Pr 1:20 ; 3:16 , 17 ; 4:8 ; 6:20-22; 9:1-4 ), whereas no prophetical or other allusions to the Saviour or the new dispensation are found among the quotations of this book in the New Testament, and unless this be such, none exist. (5) Nothing is lost as to the importance of this passage, which still remains a most ornate and also solemn and impressive teaching of inspiration on the value of wisdom. 1-4. The publicity and universality of the call contrast with the secrecy and intrigues of the wicked ( Pr 7:8 , &c.).

잠언-8-23.title: 잠언 8장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-8-23.exegesis: 22-31. Strictly, God's attributes are part of Himself. Yet, to the poetical structure of the whole passage, this commendation of wisdom is entirely consonant. In order of time all His attributes are coincident and eternal as Himself. But to set forth the importance of wisdom as devising the products of benevolence and power, it is here assigned a precedence. As it has such in divine, so should it be desired in human, affairs (compare Pr 3:19 ). possessed-- or, "created"; in either sense, the idea of precedence. in the beginning-- or simply, "beginning," in apposition with "me." before ... of old-- preceding the most ancient deeds.

잠언-10-2.title: 잠언 10장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 10 Pr 10:1-32 . Here begins the second part of the book, Pr 10:1-22:16, which, with the third, Pr 22:16-25:28, contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pr 10: 1-15:33 are mostly antithetic; and those of Pr 16:1-22:16, synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing. 1. wise [and] foolish-- as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom. maketh ... father-- or, "gladdens a father." heaviness-- or, "grief."

잠언-10-5.theologicalNote: 4. slack-- literally, "deceitful," failing of its purpose (compare Ho 7:16 ). maketh rich-- (compare Pr 10:22 ).

잠언-10-6.title: 잠언 10장 6절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-6.exegesis: 5. son-- as Pr 1:8 , 10 , and often. sleepeth-- in indolence, and not for rest. causeth shame-- literally, "is base" (compare Pr 14:35 ; 17:2 ).
잠언-10-6.theologicalNote: 5. son-- as Pr 1:8 , 10 , and often. sleepeth-- in indolence, and not for rest. causeth shame-- literally, "is base" (compare Pr 14:35 ; 17:2 ).

잠언-10-7.title: 잠언 10장 7절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-7.exegesis: 6. Blessings-- literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time ( Psa 5:9 ; 10:7 ; Ro 3:14 ), and hence has no praises (compare Pr 10:11 ).
잠언-10-7.theologicalNote: 6. Blessings-- literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time ( Psa 5:9 ; 10:7 ; Ro 3:14 ), and hence has no praises (compare Pr 10:11 ).

잠언-10-8.title: 잠언 10장 8절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-8.exegesis: 7. blessed-- literally, "for a blessing," or praise. shall rot-- literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.
잠언-10-8.theologicalNote: 7. blessed-- literally, "for a blessing," or praise. shall rot-- literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.

잠언-10-9.title: 잠언 10장 9절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-9.exegesis: 8. wise, &c.-- (compare Pr 9:8 , 9, 16 ), opposed to prating fool-- or, "fool of lips of wicked language." fall-- headlong, suddenly.
잠언-10-9.theologicalNote: 8. wise, &c.-- (compare Pr 9:8 , 9, 16 ), opposed to prating fool-- or, "fool of lips of wicked language." fall-- headlong, suddenly.

잠언-10-10.title: 잠언 10장 10절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-10.exegesis: 9. perverteth his ways-- acts deceitfully. known-- discovered and punished.
잠언-10-10.theologicalNote: 9. perverteth his ways-- acts deceitfully. known-- discovered and punished.

잠언-10-11.title: 잠언 10장 11절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-11.exegesis: 10. Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one ( Pr 6:13 ; Psa 35:19 ), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.
잠언-10-11.theologicalNote: 10. Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one ( Pr 6:13 ; Psa 35:19 ), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.

잠언-10-12.title: 잠언 10장 12절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-12.exegesis: 11. a well-- or, "source" of good to himself and others ( Joh 7:37 , 38 ). On last clause, see on Pr 10:6 .
잠언-10-12.theologicalNote: 11. a well-- or, "source" of good to himself and others ( Joh 7:37 , 38 ). On last clause, see on Pr 10:6 .

잠언-10-13.title: 잠언 10장 13절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-13.exegesis: 12. strifes-- or, "litigations." covereth-- by forgiveness and forbearance.
잠언-10-13.theologicalNote: 12. strifes-- or, "litigations." covereth-- by forgiveness and forbearance.

잠언-10-14.title: 잠언 10장 14절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-14.exegesis: 13. In the lips ... found-- hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool. void of understanding-- ( Pr 6:32 ; 7:7 ).
잠언-10-14.theologicalNote: 13. In the lips ... found-- hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool. void of understanding-- ( Pr 6:32 ; 7:7 ).

잠언-10-15.title: 잠언 10장 15절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-15.exegesis: 14. lay up knowledge-- that is, as treasures for good use. mouth ... destruction-- or, "as to the mouth," &c., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.
잠언-10-15.theologicalNote: 14. lay up knowledge-- that is, as treasures for good use. mouth ... destruction-- or, "as to the mouth," &c., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.

잠언-10-16.title: 잠언 10장 16절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-16.exegesis: 15. Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" ( 1Ti 6:17 ), or by the evils of poverty ( Pr 30:9 ), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.
잠언-10-16.theologicalNote: 15. Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" ( 1Ti 6:17 ), or by the evils of poverty ( Pr 30:9 ), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.

잠언-10-17.title: 잠언 10장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-17.exegesis: 16. The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.
잠언-10-17.theologicalNote: 16. The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.

잠언-10-18.title: 잠언 10장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-18.exegesis: 17. keepeth-- observes ( Pr 3:18 ; 4:22 ). refuseth-- or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.
잠언-10-18.theologicalNote: 17. keepeth-- observes ( Pr 3:18 ; 4:22 ). refuseth-- or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.

잠언-10-19.title: 잠언 10장 19절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-19.exegesis: 18. Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.
잠언-10-19.theologicalNote: 18. Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.

잠언-10-20.title: 잠언 10장 20절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-20.exegesis: 19. Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue ( Psa 39:1 ; Jas 1:26 ).
잠언-10-20.theologicalNote: 19. Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue ( Psa 39:1 ; Jas 1:26 ).

잠언-10-21.title: 잠언 10장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-21.exegesis: 20. Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.
잠언-10-21.theologicalNote: 20. Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.

잠언-10-22.title: 잠언 10장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-22.exegesis: 21. Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare Pr 10:11 , 17 ; Ho 4:6 ).
잠언-10-22.theologicalNote: 21. Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare Pr 10:11 , 17 ; Ho 4:6 ).

잠언-10-23.title: 잠언 10장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-23.exegesis: 22. it maketh, &c.-- "it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare Ec 2:21-23 ; 1Ti 6:9 , 10, 17).
잠언-10-23.theologicalNote: 22. it maketh, &c.-- "it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare Ec 2:21-23 ; 1Ti 6:9 , 10, 17).

잠언-10-24.title: 잠언 10장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-24.exegesis: 23. Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.
잠언-10-24.theologicalNote: 23. Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.

잠언-10-25.title: 잠언 10장 25절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-25.exegesis: 24. it-- the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.
잠언-10-25.theologicalNote: 24. it-- the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.

잠언-10-26.title: 잠언 10장 26절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-26.exegesis: 25. (Compare Psa 1:4 ; 37:9, 10, 36). righteous ... foundation-- well laid and firm ( Mt 7:24 , 25 ).
잠언-10-26.theologicalNote: 25. (Compare Psa 1:4 ; 37:9, 10, 36). righteous ... foundation-- well laid and firm ( Mt 7:24 , 25 ).

잠언-10-29.title: 잠언 10장 29절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-29.exegesis: 28. gladness-- in confidence of realizing it. expectation ... perish-- in disappointment.
잠언-10-29.theologicalNote: 28. gladness-- in confidence of realizing it. expectation ... perish-- in disappointment.

잠언-10-30.title: 잠언 10장 30절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-30.exegesis: 29. The way, &c.-- that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked ( Ho 14:9 ).
잠언-10-30.theologicalNote: 29. The way, &c.-- that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked ( Ho 14:9 ).

잠언-10-31.title: 잠언 10장 31절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-31.exegesis: 30. (Compare Pr 12:3 ; Psa 37:9-11; 102:28). earth-- or, "land of promise."
잠언-10-31.theologicalNote: 30. (Compare Pr 12:3 ; Psa 37:9-11; 102:28). earth-- or, "land of promise."

잠언-10-32.title: 잠언 10장 32절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-10-32.exegesis: 31. bringeth forth-- literally, "germinates" as a plant. froward-- (Compare Pr 2:12 , 14 ). cut off-- as an unproductive plant.
잠언-10-32.theologicalNote: 31. bringeth forth-- literally, "germinates" as a plant. froward-- (Compare Pr 2:12 , 14 ). cut off-- as an unproductive plant.

잠언-11-1.title: 잠언 11장 1절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-1.exegesis: 32. know-- regard and provide for ( Psa 1:6 ). frowardness-- all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.
잠언-11-1.theologicalNote: 32. know-- regard and provide for ( Psa 1:6 ). frowardness-- all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.

잠언-11-2.title: 잠언 11장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 11 Pr 11:1-31 . 1. (Compare Margin). The Hebrews used stones for weights. just-- complete in measure.
잠언-11-2.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 11 Pr 11:1-31 . 1. (Compare Margin). The Hebrews used stones for weights. just-- complete in measure.

잠언-11-3.title: 잠언 11장 3절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-3.exegesis: 2. Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare Pr 16:18 ; 18:12 ).
잠언-11-3.theologicalNote: 2. Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare Pr 16:18 ; 18:12 ).

잠언-11-4.title: 잠언 11장 4절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-4.exegesis: 3. guide-- to lead, as a shepherd ( Pr 6:7 ; Psa 78:52 ). perverseness-- ill-nature. destroy-- with violence.
잠언-11-4.theologicalNote: 3. guide-- to lead, as a shepherd ( Pr 6:7 ; Psa 78:52 ). perverseness-- ill-nature. destroy-- with violence.

잠언-11-5.title: 잠언 11장 5절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-5.exegesis: 4. (Compare Pr 10:2 ). wrath-- that is, of God.
잠언-11-5.theologicalNote: 4. (Compare Pr 10:2 ). wrath-- that is, of God.

잠언-11-6.title: 잠언 11장 6절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-6.exegesis: 5. direct-- or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain ( Pr 13:17 ).
잠언-11-6.theologicalNote: 5. direct-- or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain ( Pr 13:17 ).

잠언-11-7.title: 잠언 11장 7절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-7.exegesis: 6. deliver them-- that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings ( Pr 5:22 ; Psa 9:16 ).
잠언-11-7.theologicalNote: 6. deliver them-- that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings ( Pr 5:22 ; Psa 9:16 ).

잠언-11-8.title: 잠언 11장 8절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-8.exegesis: 7. expectation ... perish-- for death cuts short all his plans ( Lu 16:25 ). hope of unjust-- better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare Is 40:29 , Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.
잠언-11-8.theologicalNote: 7. expectation ... perish-- for death cuts short all his plans ( Lu 16:25 ). hope of unjust-- better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare Is 40:29 , Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.

잠언-11-9.title: 잠언 11장 9절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-9.exegesis: 8. Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare Pr 11:6 ).
잠언-11-9.theologicalNote: 8. Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare Pr 11:6 ).

잠언-11-10.title: 잠언 11장 10절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-10.exegesis: 9. (Compare Psa 35:16 ; Da 11:32 ). The just is saved by superior discernment.
잠언-11-10.theologicalNote: 9. (Compare Psa 35:16 ; Da 11:32 ). The just is saved by superior discernment.

잠언-11-11.title: 잠언 11장 11절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-11.exegesis: 10-11. The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.
잠언-11-11.theologicalNote: 10-11. The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

잠언-11-12.title: 잠언 11장 12절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-12.exegesis: 10-11. The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.
잠언-11-12.theologicalNote: 10-11. The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

잠언-11-13.title: 잠언 11장 13절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-13.exegesis: 12. despiseth-- or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise. holdeth his peace-- as if neither hearing nor telling.
잠언-11-13.theologicalNote: 12. despiseth-- or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise. holdeth his peace-- as if neither hearing nor telling.

잠언-11-14.title: 잠언 11장 14절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-14.exegesis: 13. tale-bearer-- (Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.
잠언-11-14.theologicalNote: 13. tale-bearer-- (Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.

잠언-11-15.title: 잠언 11장 15절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-15.exegesis: 14. counsel-- the art of governing ( Pr 1:5 ). counsellors-- literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.
잠언-11-15.theologicalNote: 14. counsel-- the art of governing ( Pr 1:5 ). counsellors-- literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.

잠언-11-16.title: 잠언 11장 16절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-16.exegesis: 15. (Compare Pr 6:1 ). suretiship-- (Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.
잠언-11-16.theologicalNote: 15. (Compare Pr 6:1 ). suretiship-- (Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.

잠언-11-17.title: 잠언 11장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-17.exegesis: 16. retaineth-- or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.
잠언-11-17.theologicalNote: 16. retaineth-- or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.

잠언-11-18.title: 잠언 11장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-18.exegesis: 17. merciful-- kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare Pr 24:5 ), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others. flesh-- that is, his body, by penuriousness ( Col 2:23 ).
잠언-11-18.theologicalNote: 17. merciful-- kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare Pr 24:5 ), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others. flesh-- that is, his body, by penuriousness ( Col 2:23 ).

잠언-11-19.title: 잠언 11장 19절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-19.exegesis: 18. a deceitful work-- or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away ( Pr 10:2 ; 23:5 ). sure reward-- or, "gain," as from trading ( Ho 10:12 ; Ga 6:8 , 9 ).
잠언-11-19.theologicalNote: 18. a deceitful work-- or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away ( Pr 10:2 ; 23:5 ). sure reward-- or, "gain," as from trading ( Ho 10:12 ; Ga 6:8 , 9 ).

잠언-11-21.title: 잠언 11장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-21.exegesis: 20. (Compare Pr 11:5 ). froward-- as in Pr 2:15 , opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright. in their way-- or, "conduct."
잠언-11-21.theologicalNote: 20. (Compare Pr 11:5 ). froward-- as in Pr 2:15 , opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright. in their way-- or, "conduct."

잠언-11-22.title: 잠언 11장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-22.exegesis: 21. The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship ( Psa 37:25 , 26 ).
잠언-11-22.theologicalNote: 21. The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship ( Psa 37:25 , 26 ).

잠언-11-23.title: 잠언 11장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-23.exegesis: 22. Jewels were often suspended from the nose ( Ge 24:47 ; Is 3:21 ). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.
잠언-11-23.theologicalNote: 22. Jewels were often suspended from the nose ( Ge 24:47 ; Is 3:21 ). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.

잠언-11-24.title: 잠언 11장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-24.exegesis: 23. (Compare Pr 10:28 ). wrath-- is that of God.
잠언-11-24.theologicalNote: 23. (Compare Pr 10:28 ). wrath-- is that of God.

잠언-11-25.title: 잠언 11장 25절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-11-25.exegesis: 24-31. The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23 . Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.
잠언-11-25.theologicalNote: 24-31. The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23 . Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

잠언-12-1.title: 잠언 12장 1절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-1.exegesis: 24-31. The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23 . Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.
잠언-12-1.theologicalNote: 24-31. The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23 . Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

잠언-12-2.title: 잠언 12장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 12 Pr 12:1-28 . 1. loveth knowledge-- as the fruit of instruction or training ( Pr 1:2 ). hateth reproof-- ( Pr 10:17 ). brutish-- stupid, regardless of his own welfare ( Psa 49:10 ; 73:22 ).
잠언-12-2.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 12 Pr 12:1-28 . 1. loveth knowledge-- as the fruit of instruction or training ( Pr 1:2 ). hateth reproof-- ( Pr 10:17 ). brutish-- stupid, regardless of his own welfare ( Psa 49:10 ; 73:22 ).

잠언-12-3.title: 잠언 12장 3절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-3.exegesis: CHAPTER 12 Pr 12:1-28 . 1. loveth knowledge-- as the fruit of instruction or training ( Pr 1:2 ). hateth reproof-- ( Pr 10:17 ). brutish-- stupid, regardless of his own welfare ( Psa 49:10 ; 73:22 ).
잠언-12-3.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 12 Pr 12:1-28 . 1. loveth knowledge-- as the fruit of instruction or training ( Pr 1:2 ). hateth reproof-- ( Pr 10:17 ). brutish-- stupid, regardless of his own welfare ( Psa 49:10 ; 73:22 ).

잠언-12-4.title: 잠언 12장 4절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-4.exegesis: 3. Wickedness cannot give permanent prosperity. root ... not be moved-- firm as a flourishing tree--( Psa 1:3 ; 15:5 ; Jr 17:8 ).
잠언-12-4.theologicalNote: 3. Wickedness cannot give permanent prosperity. root ... not be moved-- firm as a flourishing tree--( Psa 1:3 ; 15:5 ; Jr 17:8 ).

잠언-12-5.title: 잠언 12장 5절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-5.exegesis: 4. A virtuous woman-- in the wide sense of well-disposed to all moral duties ( Pr 31:10 ). maketh ashamed-- that is, by misconduct. rottenness-- an incurable evil.
잠언-12-5.theologicalNote: 4. A virtuous woman-- in the wide sense of well-disposed to all moral duties ( Pr 31:10 ). maketh ashamed-- that is, by misconduct. rottenness-- an incurable evil.

잠언-12-6.title: 잠언 12장 6절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-6.exegesis: 5. thoughts-- or, "purposes." are right-- literally, "are judgment," that is, true decisions. counsels-- (Compare Pr 11:14 ). deceit-- contrary to truth and honesty.
잠언-12-6.theologicalNote: 5. thoughts-- or, "purposes." are right-- literally, "are judgment," that is, true decisions. counsels-- (Compare Pr 11:14 ). deceit-- contrary to truth and honesty.

잠언-12-7.title: 잠언 12장 7절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-7.exegesis: 6. The words-- or, "expressed designs" of the wicked are for evil purposes. the mouth-- or, "words" of the righteous delivering instead of ensnaring men.
잠언-12-7.theologicalNote: 6. The words-- or, "expressed designs" of the wicked are for evil purposes. the mouth-- or, "words" of the righteous delivering instead of ensnaring men.

잠언-12-8.title: 잠언 12장 8절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-8.exegesis: 7. Such conduct brings a proper return, by the destruction of the wicked and well-being of the righteous and his family.
잠언-12-8.theologicalNote: 7. Such conduct brings a proper return, by the destruction of the wicked and well-being of the righteous and his family.

잠언-12-9.title: 잠언 12장 9절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-9.exegesis: 8. despised-- as opposed to commended ( Pr 11:12 ). perverse heart-- or, "wicked principles," as opposed to one of wisdom.
잠언-12-9.theologicalNote: 8. despised-- as opposed to commended ( Pr 11:12 ). perverse heart-- or, "wicked principles," as opposed to one of wisdom.

잠언-12-10.title: 잠언 12장 10절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-10.exegesis: 9. despised-- held in little repute, obscure ( 1Sa 18:23 ; Is 3:5 ). hath a servant-- implying some means of honest living. honoureth himself-- is self-conceited.
잠언-12-10.theologicalNote: 9. despised-- held in little repute, obscure ( 1Sa 18:23 ; Is 3:5 ). hath a servant-- implying some means of honest living. honoureth himself-- is self-conceited.

잠언-12-11.title: 잠언 12장 11절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-11.exegesis: 10. regardeth-- literally, "knoweth" ( Psa 1:6 ). mercies ... cruel-- as acts of compassion ungraciously rendered to the needy. The righteous more regards a beast than the wicked a man.
잠언-12-11.theologicalNote: 10. regardeth-- literally, "knoweth" ( Psa 1:6 ). mercies ... cruel-- as acts of compassion ungraciously rendered to the needy. The righteous more regards a beast than the wicked a man.

잠언-12-12.title: 잠언 12장 12절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-12.exegesis: 11. The idler's fate is the result of indolence and want of principle ( Pr 6:32 ; 7:7 ).
잠언-12-12.theologicalNote: 11. The idler's fate is the result of indolence and want of principle ( Pr 6:32 ; 7:7 ).

잠언-12-13.title: 잠언 12장 13절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-13.exegesis: 12. the wicked ... evil-- They love the crafty arts of deception. the root ... fruit-- their own resources supply them; or, it may be rendered: "He (God) giveth, or, sets ( Eze 17:22 ) the root of the righteous," and hence it is firm: or, the verb is impersonal; "As to the root ... it is firm" ( Pr 17:19 ).
잠언-12-13.theologicalNote: 12. the wicked ... evil-- They love the crafty arts of deception. the root ... fruit-- their own resources supply them; or, it may be rendered: "He (God) giveth, or, sets ( Eze 17:22 ) the root of the righteous," and hence it is firm: or, the verb is impersonal; "As to the root ... it is firm" ( Pr 17:19 ).

잠언-12-14.title: 잠언 12장 14절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-14.exegesis: 13-14. The wicked is snared, &c.-- The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.
잠언-12-14.theologicalNote: 13-14. The wicked is snared, &c.-- The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

잠언-12-15.title: 잠언 12장 15절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-15.exegesis: 13-14. The wicked is snared, &c.-- The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.
잠언-12-15.theologicalNote: 13-14. The wicked is snared, &c.-- The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

잠언-12-16.title: 잠언 12장 16절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-16.exegesis: 15. The way ... eyes-- The fool is self-conceited (compare Pr 12:1 ; 1:32; 10:17; Jas 3:17 ).
잠언-12-16.theologicalNote: 15. The way ... eyes-- The fool is self-conceited (compare Pr 12:1 ; 1:32; 10:17; Jas 3:17 ).

잠언-12-17.title: 잠언 12장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-17.exegesis: 16. prudent ... shame-- He is slow to denounce his insulters ( Jas 1:19 ).
잠언-12-17.theologicalNote: 16. prudent ... shame-- He is slow to denounce his insulters ( Jas 1:19 ).

잠언-12-18.title: 잠언 12장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-18.exegesis: 16. prudent ... shame-- He is slow to denounce his insulters ( Jas 1:19 ).
잠언-12-18.theologicalNote: 16. prudent ... shame-- He is slow to denounce his insulters ( Jas 1:19 ).

잠언-12-19.title: 잠언 12장 19절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-19.exegesis: 18. speaketh-- literally, "speaketh hastily," or indiscreetly ( Psa 106:33 ), as an angry man retorts harsh and provoking invectives. tongue ... health-- by soothing and gentle language.
잠언-12-19.theologicalNote: 18. speaketh-- literally, "speaketh hastily," or indiscreetly ( Psa 106:33 ), as an angry man retorts harsh and provoking invectives. tongue ... health-- by soothing and gentle language.

잠언-12-20.title: 잠언 12장 20절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-20.exegesis: 19. Words of truth are consistent, and stand all tests, while lies are soon discovered and exposed.
잠언-12-20.theologicalNote: 19. Words of truth are consistent, and stand all tests, while lies are soon discovered and exposed.

잠언-12-21.title: 잠언 12장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-21.exegesis: 20. that imagine-- or, "plan" ( Pr 3:29 ). They design a deceitful course, to which, with all its evils and dangers to others and themselves, the happiness of peace-makers is opposed (compare Mt 5:9 ; Ro 12:18 ).
잠언-12-21.theologicalNote: 20. that imagine-- or, "plan" ( Pr 3:29 ). They design a deceitful course, to which, with all its evils and dangers to others and themselves, the happiness of peace-makers is opposed (compare Mt 5:9 ; Ro 12:18 ).

잠언-12-22.title: 잠언 12장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-22.exegesis: 21. no evil-- (as in Psa 91:10 ), under God's wise limitations ( Ro 8:28 ). mischief-- as penal evil.
잠언-12-22.theologicalNote: 21. no evil-- (as in Psa 91:10 ), under God's wise limitations ( Ro 8:28 ). mischief-- as penal evil.

잠언-12-23.title: 잠언 12장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-23.exegesis: 22. deal truly-- or, "faithfully," that is, according to promises (compare Joh 3:21 ).
잠언-12-23.theologicalNote: 22. deal truly-- or, "faithfully," that is, according to promises (compare Joh 3:21 ).

잠언-12-24.title: 잠언 12장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-24.exegesis: 23. concealeth-- by his modesty ( Pr 10:14 ; 11:13 ). heart ... proclaimeth-- as his lips speak his thoughts (compare Ec 10:3 ).
잠언-12-24.theologicalNote: 23. concealeth-- by his modesty ( Pr 10:14 ; 11:13 ). heart ... proclaimeth-- as his lips speak his thoughts (compare Ec 10:3 ).

잠언-12-25.title: 잠언 12장 25절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-25.exegesis: 24. slothful-- (Compare Margin), so called because he fails to meet his promises. under tribute-- not denoting legal taxes, but the obligation of dependence.
잠언-12-25.theologicalNote: 24. slothful-- (Compare Margin), so called because he fails to meet his promises. under tribute-- not denoting legal taxes, but the obligation of dependence.

잠언-12-26.title: 잠언 12장 26절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-26.exegesis: 25. a good word-- one of comfort.
잠언-12-26.theologicalNote: 25. a good word-- one of comfort.

잠언-12-27.title: 잠언 12장 27절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-27.exegesis: 26. more excellent-- (Compare Margin); or, "more successful," while the wicked fail; or, we may read it: "The righteous guides his friend, but," &c., that is, The ability of the righteous to aid others is contrasted with the ruin to which the way of the wicked leads themselves.
잠언-12-27.theologicalNote: 26. more excellent-- (Compare Margin); or, "more successful," while the wicked fail; or, we may read it: "The righteous guides his friend, but," &c., that is, The ability of the righteous to aid others is contrasted with the ruin to which the way of the wicked leads themselves.

잠언-12-28.title: 잠언 12장 28절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-12-28.exegesis: 27. (Compare Pr 12:24 ). took in hunting-- or, "his venison." He does not improve his advantages. the substance ... precious-- or, "the wealth of a man of honor is being diligent," or "diligence." precious-- literally, "honor" ( Ec 10:1 ).
잠언-12-28.theologicalNote: 27. (Compare Pr 12:24 ). took in hunting-- or, "his venison." He does not improve his advantages. the substance ... precious-- or, "the wealth of a man of honor is being diligent," or "diligence." precious-- literally, "honor" ( Ec 10:1 ).

잠언-13-1.title: 잠언 13장 1절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-1.exegesis: 28. (Compare Pr 8:8 , 20 , &c.). A sentiment often stated; here first affirmatively, then negatively.
잠언-13-1.theologicalNote: 28. (Compare Pr 8:8 , 20 , &c.). A sentiment often stated; here first affirmatively, then negatively.

잠언-13-3.title: 잠언 13장 3절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-3.exegesis: 2. shall eat-- that is, obtain ( Pr 12:14 ). transgressors-- as in Pr 2:22 . violence-- or, "mischief" to themselves.
잠언-13-3.theologicalNote: 2. shall eat-- that is, obtain ( Pr 12:14 ). transgressors-- as in Pr 2:22 . violence-- or, "mischief" to themselves.

잠언-13-4.title: 잠언 13장 4절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-4.exegesis: 3. He ... mouth ... life-- because evil speeches may provoke violence from others. he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction-- On last clause, compare Pr 10:14 .
잠언-13-4.theologicalNote: 3. He ... mouth ... life-- because evil speeches may provoke violence from others. he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction-- On last clause, compare Pr 10:14 .

잠언-13-6.title: 잠언 13장 6절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-6.exegesis: 5. loathsome ... shame-- better, causeth shame and reproach (compare Pr 19:26 ), by slander, &c., which the righteous hates.
잠언-13-6.theologicalNote: 5. loathsome ... shame-- better, causeth shame and reproach (compare Pr 19:26 ), by slander, &c., which the righteous hates.

잠언-13-7.title: 잠언 13장 7절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-7.exegesis: 6. A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.
잠언-13-7.theologicalNote: 6. A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.

잠언-13-8.title: 잠언 13장 8절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-8.exegesis: 7. In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.
잠언-13-8.theologicalNote: 7. In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.

잠언-13-9.title: 잠언 13장 9절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-9.exegesis: 8. Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.
잠언-13-9.theologicalNote: 8. Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.

잠언-13-10.title: 잠언 13장 10절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-10.exegesis: 9. light ... lamp-- prosperity; the first, the greater, and it rejoiceth-- burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.
잠언-13-10.theologicalNote: 9. light ... lamp-- prosperity; the first, the greater, and it rejoiceth-- burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.

잠언-13-11.title: 잠언 13장 11절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-11.exegesis: 10. The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.
잠언-13-11.theologicalNote: 10. The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.

잠언-13-12.title: 잠언 13장 12절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-12.exegesis: 11. by vanity-- or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices). gathereth ... labour-- (Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.
잠언-13-12.theologicalNote: 11. by vanity-- or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices). gathereth ... labour-- (Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.

잠언-13-13.title: 잠언 13장 13절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-13.exegesis: 12. desire cometh-- is realized. a tree of life-- or, "cause of happiness."
잠언-13-13.theologicalNote: 12. desire cometh-- is realized. a tree of life-- or, "cause of happiness."

잠언-13-14.title: 잠언 13장 14절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-14.exegesis: 13. the word-- that is, of advice, or, instruction (compare Pr 10:27 ; 11:31 ).
잠언-13-14.theologicalNote: 13. the word-- that is, of advice, or, instruction (compare Pr 10:27 ; 11:31 ).

잠언-13-15.title: 잠언 13장 15절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-15.exegesis: 14. (Compare Pr 10:11 ). fountain-- or, "source of life." to depart-- (compare Pr 1:2-4 ), or, "for departing," &c., and so gives life.
잠언-13-15.theologicalNote: 14. (Compare Pr 10:11 ). fountain-- or, "source of life." to depart-- (compare Pr 1:2-4 ), or, "for departing," &c., and so gives life.

잠언-13-16.title: 잠언 13장 16절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-16.exegesis: 15. Right perception and action secure good will, while evil ways are difficult as a stony road. The wicked left of God find punishment of sin in sinning. hard-- or, "harsh" (compare Hebrew: De 21:4 ; Jr 5:15 ).
잠언-13-16.theologicalNote: 15. Right perception and action secure good will, while evil ways are difficult as a stony road. The wicked left of God find punishment of sin in sinning. hard-- or, "harsh" (compare Hebrew: De 21:4 ; Jr 5:15 ).

잠언-13-17.title: 잠언 13장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-17.exegesis: 16. dealeth-- acts with foresight. a fool ... folly-- for want of caution.
잠언-13-17.theologicalNote: 16. dealeth-- acts with foresight. a fool ... folly-- for want of caution.

잠언-13-18.title: 잠언 13장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-18.exegesis: 17. A wicked-- or, "unfaithful" messenger falleth into mischief-- or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.
잠언-13-18.theologicalNote: 17. A wicked-- or, "unfaithful" messenger falleth into mischief-- or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.

잠언-13-20.title: 잠언 13장 20절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-20.exegesis: 19. Self-denial, which fools will not endure, is essential to success.
잠언-13-20.theologicalNote: 19. Self-denial, which fools will not endure, is essential to success.

잠언-13-21.title: 잠언 13장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-21.exegesis: 20. The benefits of good and evil of bad society are contrasted.
잠언-13-21.theologicalNote: 20. The benefits of good and evil of bad society are contrasted.

잠언-13-22.title: 잠언 13장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-22.exegesis: 21. (Compare Pr 11:31 ). good ... repaid-- or, "He (God) will repay good."
잠언-13-22.theologicalNote: 21. (Compare Pr 11:31 ). good ... repaid-- or, "He (God) will repay good."

잠언-13-23.title: 잠언 13장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-23.exegesis: 22. wealth ... just-- While good men's estates remain in their families, God so orders that the gains of sinners enure to the just (compare Pr 28:8 ; Psa 37:18 , 22, 26 , &c.).
잠언-13-23.theologicalNote: 22. wealth ... just-- While good men's estates remain in their families, God so orders that the gains of sinners enure to the just (compare Pr 28:8 ; Psa 37:18 , 22, 26 , &c.).

잠언-13-24.title: 잠언 13장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-24.exegesis: 23. The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.
잠언-13-24.theologicalNote: 23. The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.

잠언-13-25.title: 잠언 13장 25절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-13-25.exegesis: 24. spareth-- or, "withholds." rod-- of correction. hateth-- or, acts as if he hated him (compare Pr 3:12 ; 8:36 ). chasteneth ... betimes-- or, "diligently seeks for him all useful discipline."
잠언-13-25.theologicalNote: 24. spareth-- or, "withholds." rod-- of correction. hateth-- or, acts as if he hated him (compare Pr 3:12 ; 8:36 ). chasteneth ... betimes-- or, "diligently seeks for him all useful discipline."

잠언-14-1.title: 잠언 14장 1절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-14-1.exegesis: 25. The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.
잠언-14-1.theologicalNote: 25. The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.

잠언-14-2.title: 잠언 14장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-14-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 14 Pr 14:1-35 . 1. Every wise, &c.-- literally, "The wisdoms" (compare Pr 9:1 ) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech. buildeth ... house-- increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.
잠언-14-2.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 14 Pr 14:1-35 . 1. Every wise, &c.-- literally, "The wisdoms" (compare Pr 9:1 ) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech. buildeth ... house-- increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.

잠언-14-3.title: 잠언 14장 3절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-14-3.exegesis: 2. uprightness-- is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature ( Pr 2:15 ; 3:32) of despising Him and His law.
잠언-14-3.theologicalNote: 2. uprightness-- is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature ( Pr 2:15 ; 3:32) of despising Him and His law.

잠언-14-4.title: 잠언 14장 4절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-14-4.exegesis: 3. rod of pride-- that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

잠언-20-12.title: 잠언 20장 12절 역사문법적 주해

잠언-20-12.theologicalNote: 11. The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare Mt 7:16 ).

잠언-20-13.theologicalNote: 12. Hence, of course, God will know all you do ( Psa 94:9 ).

잠언-20-15.theologicalNote: 14. when ... his way-- implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

잠언-20-16.theologicalNote: 15. The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare Pr 3:14-16 ).

잠언-20-17.title: 잠언 20장 17절 역사문법적 주해

잠언-20-18.title: 잠언 20장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-20-18.exegesis: 17. Bread ... sweet-- either as unlawfully ( Pr 9:17 ) or easily obtained. mouth ... gravel-- well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

잠언-20-19.theologicalNote: 18. (Compare Pr 15:22 ). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

잠언-20-22.theologicalNote: 21. gotten hastily-- contrary to God's providence ( Pr 28:20 ), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare Pr 20:17 ).

잠언-20-25.theologicalNote: 24. Man's goings-- literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man." a man-- any common man. understand-- or, "perceive."

잠언-20-26.exegesis: 25. devoureth ... holy-- or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

잠언-20-28.theologicalNote: 27. The spirit ... Lord-- Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare Pr 20:5 ; Pr 18:8 , 17 ; 1Co 2:11 ).

잠언-20-30.theologicalNote: 29. The glory of young men ... the beauty of old men-- Each age has its peculiar excellence ( Pr 16:31 ).

잠언-21-5.exegesis: 4. high look-- (Compare Margin; Psa 131:1 ). proud heart-- or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Psa 101:5 ). ploughing-- better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity ( Pr 20:20 ); hence joy or delight.
잠언-21-5.theologicalNote: 4. high look-- (Compare Margin; Psa 131:1 ). proud heart-- or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Psa 101:5 ). ploughing-- better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity ( Pr 20:20 ); hence joy or delight.

잠언-21-6.theologicalNote: 5. The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare Pr 19:2 ).

잠언-21-8.exegesis: 7. robbery-- or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. shall destroy-- literally, "cut with a saw" ( 1Ki 7:9 ), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. to do judgment-- what is just and right.
잠언-21-8.theologicalNote: 7. robbery-- or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. shall destroy-- literally, "cut with a saw" ( 1Ki 7:9 ), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. to do judgment-- what is just and right.

잠언-21-13.theologicalNote: 12. (Compare Psa 37:35-38; 73:17, 20). house-- family or interests. overthroweth-- either supply "God" (compare Pr 10:24 ), or the word is used impersonally.

잠언-21-14.theologicalNote: 13. The principles of retribution, often taught (compare Psa 18:26 ; Mt 7:1-12 ).

잠언-21-27.theologicalNote: 26. The sin of covetousness marks the sluggard, as the virtue of benevolence the righteous.

잠언-21-28.theologicalNote: 27. God regards the heart, and hypocrisy is more odious than open inconsistency. wicked mind-- or, "design" ( Pr 1:4 ).

잠언-21-30.theologicalNote: 29. hardeneth his face-- is obstinate. directeth ... way-- considers it, and acts advisedly.

잠언-21-31.theologicalNote: 30-31. Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid ( Pr 19:21 ; Psa 20:7 ; 33:17 ).

잠언-22-1.theologicalNote: 30-31. Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid ( Pr 19:21 ; Psa 20:7 ; 33:17 ).

잠언-22-8.theologicalNote: 7. The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare Pr 19:6 ; 21:14 , &c.).

잠언-22-9.theologicalNote: 8. (Compare Pr 11:18 ; Psa 109:16-20 ; Ga 6:7 , 8 ). the rod ... fail-- His power to do evil will be destroyed.

잠언-26-11.theologicalNote: 10. Various versions of this are proposed (compare Margin). Better perhaps-- "Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. transgressors-- may be rendered "vagrants." 잠언-26-12.title: 잠언 26장 12절 역사문법적 주해

잠언-26-12.theologicalNote: 11. returneth ... folly-- Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

잠언-26-13.title: 잠언 26장 13절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-13.exegesis: 12. The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.
잠언-26-13.theologicalNote: 12. The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.

잠언-26-17.title: 잠언 26장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-17.exegesis: 16. The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.
잠언-26-17.theologicalNote: 16. The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.

잠언-26-18.title: 잠언 26장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-18.exegesis: 17. meddleth-- as in Pr 20:19 ; 24:21 ; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.
잠언-26-18.theologicalNote: 17. meddleth-- as in Pr 20:19 ; 24:21 ; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.

잠언-26-21.title: 잠언 26장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-21.exegesis: 20-21. The talebearers foster ( Pr 16:28 ), and the contentious excite, strife.
잠언-26-21.theologicalNote: 20-21. The talebearers foster ( Pr 16:28 ), and the contentious excite, strife.

잠언-26-22.title: 잠언 26장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-22.exegesis: 20-21. The talebearers foster ( Pr 16:28 ), and the contentious excite, strife.
잠언-26-22.theologicalNote: 20-21. The talebearers foster ( Pr 16:28 ), and the contentious excite, strife.

잠언-26-24.title: 잠언 26장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-24.exegesis: 23. Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.
잠언-26-24.theologicalNote: 23. Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.

잠언-26-25.title: 잠언 26장 25절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-25.exegesis: 24. dissembleth-- though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.
잠언-26-25.theologicalNote: 24. dissembleth-- though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.

잠언-26-26.title: 잠언 26장 26절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-26.exegesis: 25. Sentiment of Pr 26:24 carried out. seven abominations in his heart-- that is, very many (compare Pr 24:16 ).
잠언-26-26.theologicalNote: 25. Sentiment of Pr 26:24 carried out. seven abominations in his heart-- that is, very many (compare Pr 24:16 ).

잠언-26-27.title: 잠언 26장 27절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-27.exegesis: 26-27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13 ; Psa 7:16 ; 9:17 , &c.).
잠언-26-27.theologicalNote: 26-27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13 ; Psa 7:16 ; 9:17 , &c.).

잠언-26-28.title: 잠언 26장 28절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-26-28.exegesis: 26-27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13 ; Psa 7:16 ; 9:17 , &c.).
잠언-26-28.theologicalNote: 26-27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13 ; Psa 7:16 ; 9:17 , &c.).

잠언-27-1.title: 잠언 27장 1절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-1.exegesis: 28. Men hate those they injure. A lying tongue-- "lips" for the persons (compare Pr 4:24 ; Psa 12:3 ).
잠언-27-1.theologicalNote: 28. Men hate those they injure. A lying tongue-- "lips" for the persons (compare Pr 4:24 ; Psa 12:3 ).

잠언-27-2.title: 잠언 27장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 27 Pr 27:1-27 . 1. Do not confide implicitly in your plans ( Pr 16:9 ; 19:21 ; Jas 4:13-15 ).
잠언-27-2.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 27 Pr 27:1-27 . 1. Do not confide implicitly in your plans ( Pr 16:9 ; 19:21 ; Jas 4:13-15 ).

잠언-27-4.title: 잠언 27장 4절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-4.exegesis: 3. heavy-- The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. a fool's wrath-- is unreasonable and excessive.
잠언-27-4.theologicalNote: 3. heavy-- The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. a fool's wrath-- is unreasonable and excessive.

잠언-27-5.title: 잠언 27장 5절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-5.exegesis: 4. envy-- or, "jealousy" (compare Margin; Pr 6:34 ), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.
잠언-27-5.theologicalNote: 4. envy-- or, "jealousy" (compare Margin; Pr 6:34 ), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.

잠언-27-6.title: 잠언 27장 6절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-6.exegesis: 5-6. secret love-- not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.
잠언-27-6.theologicalNote: 5-6. secret love-- not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

잠언-27-7.title: 잠언 27장 7절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-7.exegesis: 5-6. secret love-- not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.
잠언-27-7.theologicalNote: 5-6. secret love-- not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

잠언-27-8.title: 잠언 27장 8절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-8.exegesis: 7. The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.
잠언-27-8.theologicalNote: 7. The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.

잠언-27-9.title: 잠언 27장 9절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-9.exegesis: 8. Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.
잠언-27-9.theologicalNote: 8. Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.

잠언-27-10.title: 잠언 27장 10절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-10.exegesis: 9. rejoice the heart-- the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. sweetness ... counsel-- or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."
잠언-27-10.theologicalNote: 9. rejoice the heart-- the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. sweetness ... counsel-- or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."

잠언-27-11.title: 잠언 27장 11절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-11.exegesis: 10. Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.
잠언-27-11.theologicalNote: 10. Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.

잠언-27-12.title: 잠언 27장 12절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-12.exegesis: 11. The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.
잠언-27-12.theologicalNote: 11. The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.

잠언-27-15.title: 잠언 27장 15절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-15.exegesis: 14. Excessive zeal in praising raises suspicions of selfishness.
잠언-27-15.theologicalNote: 14. Excessive zeal in praising raises suspicions of selfishness.

잠언-27-16.title: 잠언 27장 16절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-16.exegesis: 15. (Compare Pr 19:13 ). very ... day-- literally, "a day of showers."
잠언-27-16.theologicalNote: 15. (Compare Pr 19:13 ). very ... day-- literally, "a day of showers."

잠언-27-17.title: 잠언 27장 17절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-17.exegesis: 16. hideth-- or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. the ointment of his right hand-- the organ of power ( Psa 17:7 ; 18:35 ). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.
잠언-27-17.theologicalNote: 16. hideth-- or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. the ointment of his right hand-- the organ of power ( Psa 17:7 ; 18:35 ). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.

잠언-27-18.title: 잠언 27장 18절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-18.exegesis: 17. a man sharpeneth ... friend-- that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.
잠언-27-18.theologicalNote: 17. a man sharpeneth ... friend-- that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.

잠언-27-19.title: 잠언 27장 19절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-19.exegesis: 18. Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.
잠언-27-19.theologicalNote: 18. Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.

잠언-27-20.title: 잠언 27장 20절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-20.exegesis: 19. We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.
잠언-27-20.theologicalNote: 19. We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.

잠언-27-21.title: 잠언 27장 21절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-21.exegesis: 20. Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.
잠언-27-21.theologicalNote: 20. Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.

잠언-27-22.title: 잠언 27장 22절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-22.exegesis: 21. Praise tests character. a man to his praise-- according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.
잠언-27-22.theologicalNote: 21. Praise tests character. a man to his praise-- according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.

잠언-27-23.title: 잠언 27장 23절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-23.exegesis: 22. The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.
잠언-27-23.theologicalNote: 22. The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.

잠언-27-24.title: 잠언 27장 24절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-27-24.exegesis: 23-24. flocks-- constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated ( Pr 23:5 ).
잠언-27-24.theologicalNote: 23-24. flocks-- constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated ( Pr 23:5 ).

잠언-27-25.title: 잠언 27장 25절 역사문법적 주해

잠언-27-25.theologicalNote: 23-24. flocks-- constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated ( Pr 23:5 ).

잠언-27-26.exegesis: 25-27. The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Psa 65:9-13 ). The hay appeareth-- literally, "Grass appeareth" ( Job 40:15 ; Psa 104:14 ).
잠언-27-26.theologicalNote: 25-27. The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Psa 65:9-13 ). The hay appeareth-- literally, "Grass appeareth" ( Job 40:15 ; Psa 104:14 ).

잠언-28-2.title: 잠언 28장 2절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-28-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 28 Pr 28:1-28 . 1. A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold ( Pr 14:26 ; Psa 27:1 ).
잠언-28-2.theologicalNote: CHAPTER 28 Pr 28:1-28 . 1. A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold ( Pr 14:26 ; Psa 27:1 ).

잠언-28-3.title: 잠언 28장 3절 역사문법적 주해
잠언-28-3.exegesis: 2. Anarchy producing contending rulers shortens the reign of each. but by a man ... prolonged-- or, "by a man of understanding--that is, a good ruler--he who knows or regards the right, that is, a good citizen, shall prolong (his days)." Good rulers are a blessing to the people. Bad government as a punishment for evil is contrasted with good as blessing to the good.
잠언-28-3.theologicalNote: 2.
